stem: A branch tied beneath a trellis begins to crease sharply at one contact point while the tip remains vigorous. What is the best LST adjustment?
choices: Tighten the existing tie so the branch remains fixed at the intended height while new tissue strengthens around the contact point.
Redistribute support and reduce the local bend angle while preserving the intended canopy position.
Top the plant above the crease because removing apical demand is the most reliable way to prevent further mechanical damage.
Leave the branch unchanged until growth slows because a vigorous tip indicates the crease is not yet affecting tissue function.
rationale: Low-stress training should redistribute growth with controlled mechanical load. Concentrated pressure or sharp bends should be corrected before tissue injury progresses.
